scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to let my 7-year-old brother stay up late watching a movie with my friend instead of going to bed on time. My mom got mad at me because she said I should have made him go to bed, and she thinks it's not good for him to miss sleep. I, on the other hand, think that since he's 7, he should understand the consequences of staying up late and that missing a couple of hours of sleep isn't a big deal, especially since he can put himself to bed. First, I need to understand why sleep is important for kids his age. I know that kids need more sleep than adults because their bodies and brains are still developing. Missing out on sleep can make them cranky, affect their ability to focus, and even impact their growth. So, in that sense, my mom is right to be concerned. But then, I also think that part of growing up is learning to handle these kinds of situations. If I always force him to go to bed, he might not learn how to manage his own time or understand the consequences of his actions. Plus, in this case, he was already awake and wanted to watch the movie with us. Making him go to bed would have probably led to a tantrum, which would have been embarrassing and exhausting for everyone involved. I also consider the fact that my friend was over, and we were just having a good time. My friend thinks my brother is cute and always hype him up, which is nice. But I also don't want my brother to feel left out or upset if he can't join in on the fun. On the other hand, I don't want to set a precedent where he can always stay up late just because he wants to hang out with me and my friends. Another thing to think about is the long-term effects. If I let him stay up late occasionally, is that really going to harm him? Or is it better to be consistent with bedtime routines to ensure he gets enough sleep regularly? I guess it's a balance between flexibility and consistency. I also wonder about the role of forgiveness and how I treat people, as I mentioned earlier. If I'm too strict with him, does that affect how I see my responsibilities towards him? Or does being flexible show that I care about his feelings and want to make sure he's happy? In the end, I'm torn between respecting my mom's authority and understanding the importance of sleep for my brother, and wanting to give him some flexibility and teach him responsibility. I need to figure out where the line is and how to handle similar situations in the future.
